findings.title: Audit retention and directory answers are not validated, so setup can print a command that review.js rejects
findings.impact: The setup accepts any non-empty text for retention days. A value like 'abc', '-1', '7.5' or '5000' is placed in the printed command unchanged. review.js accepts only /^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/, and the prompt states a 0–3650 range. A user who follows the wizard gets a command that fails with INVALID_CLI_CONFIG. The wizard also says an absolute directory path is required, but it does not check that.

findings.title: Printed command is joined with spaces without quoting
findings.impact: The command is built with command.join(' '). Paths, model IDs or audit directories that contain spaces or shell metacharacters produce a command that cannot be pasted and run. The output directory defaults to join(cwd, 'triview-setup'), so a cwd with spaces breaks the printed --policy path.

findings.title: Single-adapter setup drops adapter config from the printed command
findings.impact: For one shared generic adapter, the wizard collects or loads a config and uses it to load the adapter. It never writes that config to a file, and the printed command has no --adapter-config. review.js then runs the adapter with {}, so the adapter misconfigures or fails. The test on line 52 asserts that config is passed to loadAdapter, but the command assertion on lines 58-59 does not include it.

findings.title: Adapter settings entered at the prompt may include credentials and are written as plaintext with default permissions
findings.impact: Users type arbitrary key = value settings, such as API keys or tokens. These are echoed in the terminal and written to routes.json. The file is created with default umask permissions, typically world-readable, in ./triview-setup, which may be committed or shared. The wizard does not warn about this or restrict file mode.

findings.title: Local-only answer is not reconciled with a detected Claude Code assistant
findings.impact: If the user says code must not go to AI servers, the wizard still accepts a detected Claude Code assistant. It labels that assistant as hosted dataHandling and writes a local-only policy that names the hosted provider. The generated config is inconsistent and will likely be refused at policy validation or preflight, with no guidance. The data-handling answer and the assistant choice are never cross-checked.
